note: Real reference-list entries, written out in full, to measure the one query shape that has never been measured: a whole reference string handed to Crossref's query.bibliographic. The inline path was measured on surnames + the SENTENCE's words (eval/fabrication, 0/36 false alarms); a resolved marker replaces those words with the entry itself, and that substitution can only be justified by a number.
realSelection: The same standard as eval/fabrication/references.json — independently, famously real, spread across decades and disciplines — and rendered in the style a writer using that citation system would actually type. Titles and venues are written from knowledge of the literature, NOT copied from a Crossref result, so a miss here is a finding about the query rather than a labelling artefact.
fabricatedConstruction: The same ten invented pairs the inline check was measured on, given the reference-list entry a language model would produce for them: a plausible journal, a round recent year, and a title that restates the claim. If the entry string makes one of these corroborate, the entry query is buying recall at the cost of the only thing that matters.
